intro: Saulkrasti is a town on Latvia's Gulf of Riga coast, north of Riga. In its Pabaži neighbourhood stands an old tree, a lime by its bark and leaves, whose trunk has opened into two tall hollows, one above the other, their edges rolled into smooth lips of new wood. A reader photographed it and sent it to us without a word; we would like to know its name.
meta_description: A hollow old lime at Pabaži, Saulkrasti, on Latvia's coast, sent by a reader: where it stands and what we know so far.

trees.name: The Hollow Lime of Pabaži
trees.how_to_recognise: Inside a low wooden fence: a grey, furrowed trunk opened by two tall dark hollows, one above the other, their edges rolled into smooth pale lips of new wood.
trees.access: On open ground at Pabaži, where the reader stood at the fence around it. A fence keeps visitors off the roots.
trees.story:
A reader sent us this tree from Pabaži, part of Saulkrasti on Latvia's Gulf of Riga coast, with no words at all. The photograph says enough.

The trunk has opened. Two tall, dark hollows run up through the middle of it, one above the other, divided by a narrow bridge of wood, and around them the living tree has rolled its bark inward in thick, smooth lips of pale new growth, the way an old tree seals the edges of a wound it cannot close. Part of the inner wall is bare and red-brown. Outside, the bark is grey and furrowed, a low wooden fence stands round the foot, and parkland trees fill the ground behind.

By its bark and the heart-shaped leaves at the edge of the picture it looks like a lime, and photographers on Wikimedia Commons label the limes at this spot Katrīnas liepas, Catherine's lindens. We would like a reader to confirm the species and tell us the story behind the name. We have no name, age or girth for it yet. If you know this tree, or there is a sign nearby that tells its story, send us a photograph and we will add it.

Look into the lower hollow from the fence.
